tagline: The Home Depot is the world's largest home improvement retailer based on net sales for fiscal 2025.
hero_kpi_rationale: Home Depot dominates the home improvement market, where comparable store sales (SSS) is the primary indicator of organic growth and commercial health, directly reflecting customer traffic and residential demand dynamics.
company_description: The Home Depot, Inc. operates as a home improvement retailer in the United States and internationally. It sells various building materials, home improvement products, lawn and garden products, and décor products, as well as facilities maintenance, repair, and operations products. The company also offers installation services for flooring, water heaters, baths, garage doors, cabinets, cabinet makeovers, countertops, sheds, furnaces and central air systems, and windows. In addition, it provides tool and equipment rental services. The company serves consumers, such as do-it-yourself homeowners and do-it-for-me customers; and professional renovators/remodelers, general contractors, small to medium homebuilders, maintenance professionals, handymen, property managers, building service contractors and specialty tradespeople, such as electricians, landscapers, plumbers, painters, pool contractors, and roofers. It sells its products through websites and its mobile applications, including homedepot.com; homedepot.ca and homedepot.com.mx; blinds.com, justblinds.com, and americanblinds.com for custom window coverings; thecompanystore.com, an online site for textiles and décor products; hdsuppl

kpis.name: Comparable Store Sales
kpis.explanation: Growth in sales at stores open for more than one year, excluding the effects of openings or closings.
kpis.description: Comparable sales rose 0.3% in 2025, vs -1.8% in 2024, marking a rebound after a period of slowdown in the housing market.
kpis.signal: Positive organic growth after two negative years.

kpis.name: Net Sales
kpis.explanation: Total sales of merchandise and services after deductions.
kpis.description: Net sales reached $164.7 billion in 2025, up 3.2%, driven by SRS and GMS (+$6.3 billion) despite an extra-day effect in 2024.
kpis.signal: Growth driven by acquisitions and comparable sales.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.description: Operating margin fell to 12.7% in 2025 vs 13.5% in 2024, due to cost inflation and post-acquisition investments.
kpis.signal: Slight marginal contraction despite sales growth.

kpis.name: Inventory Turnover
kpis.explanation: Number of times inventory is renewed during the year.
kpis.description: Inventory turnover declined from 4.7 to 4.4, reflecting higher inventory levels in anticipation of demand or tied to acquisition integrations.

kpis.name: Operating Cash Flow
kpis.explanation: Cash generated by the company's core activity.
kpis.description: Operating cash flow stood at $16.3 billion, used for dividends, debt repayment and capex.
kpis.signal: Very strong operating cash flow, despite investments.

kpis.name: Number of Stores
kpis.explanation: Total number of stores open worldwide.
kpis.description: 10 new stores in the United States and 2 in Mexico brought the total to 2,359 stores in 2025.
kpis.signal: Moderate growth of the physical network.

kpis.name: Return on Invested Capital
kpis.explanation: Measure of profitability on equity and debt used in the business.
kpis.description: ROIC fell to 25.7% in 2025 vs 31.3% in 2024, due to higher debt and a pause in share buybacks.
kpis.signal: ROIC declining after the GMS acquisition.

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.description: Net income extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 8 reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Net income of $14.156 billion in the latest fiscal year (FY2025).

kpis.name: Dividend per Share
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share paid, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last 7 reported fiscal years.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of $2.33 in the latest year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned (Dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last 4 reported fiscal years.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of $9.152 billion in the latest year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout Ratio = Dividends Paid / Net Income, calculated over the last 4 fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Share of net income distributed as dividends: 64.7% in the latest year.

risks.title: Intense Competition from Retailers and Marketplaces
risks.summary: Home Depot operates in a highly fragmented and competitive sector, facing traditional retailers, direct suppliers, and online marketplaces (Amazon, etc.). Market fragmentation and the evolution of distribution channels (reseller marketplaces) create growing pressure on market share and margins.
risks.score_rationale: Risk mentioned at the very start of Item 1A ('highly competitive, highly fragmented'). Moderate but repeated language. Stable but structural trend. High weighting: direct competition from retailers and emergence of reseller marketplaces threaten the dominant position.

risks.title: Dependence on the Global Supply Chain
risks.summary: Home Depot maintains sourcing offices in China, Vietnam, India, Taiwan and Mexico. Trade tariffs, trade restrictions and geopolitical tensions threaten supply costs and product availability. Supply chain diversification remains a major strategic challenge.
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly cited in forward-looking statements (tariffs, trade policy, supply chain diversification). Urgent language ('efforts and ability to continue to diversify'). Trend up: tariffs and trade tensions mentioned as future risks. High weighting for an importing retailer.

risks.title: Risks Related to SRS and GMS Acquisitions
risks.summary: The acquisition of SRS (roofing, landscape, pool) and its sub-acquisition of GMS (drywall, ceilings, steel framing) represents a major expansion into specialty Pros. Risks include operational integration, realizing expected synergies, and managing 1,250+ new locations with different commercial models.
risks.score_rationale: Major acquisitions (SRS in fiscal 2024, GMS in fiscal 2025) with 1,250+ locations. Forward-looking statements explicitly mention 'ability to recognize the anticipated benefits'. Cautious language on integration. Trend new/up: recent acquisitions. High weighting: strategic transformation of the portfolio.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and Customer Data Protection
risks.summary: Home Depot operates major e-commerce sites (homedepot.com, hdsupply.com, srsdistribution.com, etc.) and collects sensitive customer data. Cyberattacks, data theft and technology disruptions threaten operational continuity, reputation and regulatory compliance (particularly after past sector incidents).
risks.score_rationale: Item 1C dedicated to cybersecurity (page 22). Forward-looking statements explicitly cite 'cybersecurity events' as a disruption risk. Increasingly important language. Trend up: cybersecurity is becoming a regulatory and operational issue. High weighting for an omnichannel retailer with massive data.

risks.title: Labor Availability and Costs
risks.summary: Home Depot employs tens of thousands of associates across its 2,359 stores and SRS network. Labor shortages, wage increases, union disputes and high turnover threaten customer service quality and operating margins. The 'Drive our core and culture' strategy depends on talent retention.
risks.score_rationale: Forward-looking statements mention 'cost and availability of labor' and 'labor disputes' as risks. Moderate but explicit concern. Trend up: post-COVID labor market tensions. High weighting: 2,359 stores + 1,250 SRS locations = massive workforce.

risks.title: Demand Volatility and Economic Cycles
risks.summary: Demand for home improvement products depends heavily on economic cycles, mortgage rates, availability of housing credit and consumer confidence. Economic slowdowns, rate hikes or credit crises reduce renovation spending and impact comparable sales.
risks.score_rationale: Forward-looking statements cite 'macroeconomic conditions', 'state of the housing and home improvement markets', 'state of the credit markets'. Repeated, nuanced language. Stable but cyclical trend. High weighting: DIY/DIFM demand sensitive to mortgage rates and household confidence.

risks.title: Regulatory and Environmental Compliance
risks.summary: Home Depot operates under federal, state and local regulations (EPA, EH&S) in the US, Canada and Mexico. Regulatory changes (taxes, environment, labor, sustainability) and executive orders create compliance risks, fines and operational adjustments. Sustainability and human capital management expectations are increasing.
risks.score_rationale: Forward-looking statements mention 'legal and regulatory changes', 'executive orders', 'changes to tax laws'. Moderate language. Stable but rising trend (ESG, EPA). Moderate-to-high weighting: multi-jurisdiction retailer (US, Canada, Mexico) with EH&S obligations.

risks.title: Supply Chain Disruptions and External Events
risks.summary: Home Depot relies on a complex distribution and fulfillment center network. Natural disasters, climate change, geopolitical conflicts, health crises and logistical disruptions threaten supply continuity and on-shelf product availability (critical for the strategy).
risks.score_rationale: Forward-looking statements cite 'events that could disrupt our business, supply chain, technology infrastructure' (tariffs, natural disasters, climate change, public health, labor disputes). Moderate concern. Trend up: accumulation of risks (geopolitical, climate). High weighting for a complex logistics network.
